title: Audit and migrate nested Auto Layout frames to simplified frame patterns
creator: Ava Chen
description: Background: Over the last two years the Figma library accumulated many components that rely on nested Auto Layout frames (3+ levels) to satisfy very specific edge cases. These patterns increase authoring complexity, cause inconsistent token overrides, and lead to broken instances when variants or spacing tokens change. Goal: Audit the library for deeply nested Auto Layout patterns across buttons, tables, and chart components and migrate them to a simplified, single-direction frame pattern where possible. Reduce variant depth, standardize spacing tokens, and create a migration plan that preserves existing instances via alias components or compatibility shims until apps can be updated.
tasks: Inventory: Run a component scan and produce a spreadsheet of components with >2 nested auto-layout frames (buttons, rows, table cells, chart legends). Link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/FIGMA-AUTO-LAYOUT-AUDIT
Define target patterns: Document 3 canonical patterns (single-axis horizontal, single-axis vertical, stacked grid) with token mapping and example instances.
Prototype refactor: Pick one complex table and one multi-state button, refactor into simplified frames, update tokens, and record layout diffs.
Compatibility plan: Author alias components or 'compat' variants to match existing instances so existing files don't break on publish.
Create automated QA checks: Figma plugin checks for layout depth and missing token maps to run pre-publish.
Run staged publish: Alpha (internal components team) -> Beta (product teams) -> Global, with rollback gating in Console release notes.
Update docs: Add migration guidelines, before/after screenshots, and handbook section for designers and engineers. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DS/pages/Autolayout+Migration
acceptance_criteria: Top 40 most-used components have depth <=2 Auto Layout frames or documented justification for deeper nesting.
No visual regressions in sampled product pages (dashboard table, settings list, Signup CTA) after alias compatibility publish.
Tokens: spacing tokens referenced in refactored components match Design Token spec and are resolvable by CLI token export.
Publish: library publish completes with CI preflight checks and no failing gating rules for the components targeted in this ticket.
Handbook: migration guide created and shared in #design-system with approval from Platform PM and two engineering reviewers.
